workflows.title: Public liveness and client configuration
agent_tools: None; create_system_router closes over injected PublicConfiguration
permissions: Public endpoints; no identity, course, learner, or cloud-read authorization is attempted
state_changes: None in persistence or browser storage; config response permits public caching for 300 seconds
success: GET /api/health returns fixed service liveness; it is hidden from OpenAPI
GET /api/healthz returns status, version and sorted allowed models
GET /api/config returns injected default_model, agent_model, allowed_models and version
failure_retry: These routes do not test cloud readiness, worker health or model availability
Reads can be repeated; no job, cancellation or retry state exists

workflows.title: Administrator-managed student assignments
agent_tools: None; Cosmos directory, invitation and course membership persistence
permissions: require_admin checks the active account role, not an institute or tenant scope registry
Students and teachers cannot read this assignment directory or replace studentIds
Only active or invited student directory candidates may be saved; promoted invitation aliases are normalized for display
state_changes: PUT replaces course studentIds and updatedAt using the submitted ETag
Agent-list caches are invalidated; no browser storage is written by the router
success: GET /api/agents/{agent_id}/students returns sorted directory candidates, current assignments and revision, retaining unavailable assignments as removable placeholders
PUT the same path deduplicates submitted IDs, validates candidates and revision, patches the roster and returns its new revision
failure_retry: Missing course is 404; stale revision or Cosmos 412 is 409: reload, reconcile and resubmit
Unavailable candidate IDs are 422; backend failures become 503
A repeated successful PUT with the old revision conflicts rather than silently overwriting later changes; no cancellation endpoint

workflows.title: Teacher membership and compatibility member mutations
actors: Active course owners and assigned teachers
agent_tools: None; membership persistence and cache invalidation
permissions: require_manager rejects students and mismatched requester_id, then applies ordinary course access
A course teacher need not be the owner to add a teacher or remove a teacher-only member
Adding a student requires administrator role and a valid student directory entry; removing anyone currently in studentIds also requires administrator role
The teacher-add branch does not validate the target account's existence or teacher role
state_changes: POST adds teacherIds or studentIds; DELETE invokes both teacher and student removal
Agent-list and applicable teacher-scope caches are invalidated; no browser state is changed
success: GET /api/agents/{agent_id}/members returns teacherIds and studentIds
POST the same path adds the requested membership type
DELETE /api/agents/{agent_id}/members/{target_user_id} removes the target from both arrays
failure_retry: Identity or role denial is 403; missing course is 404; storage errors are mapped to 409/503
DELETE is two persistence operations, not an atomic roster replacement; partial success is possible
These compatibility mutations expose no client revision or cancellation contract; re-read membership after an uncertain write

workflows.title: Manage-code connection and caller-scoped TA listing
actors: Active students, teachers, administrators and superadministrators
agent_tools: None; manage-code lookup and main.azure_agents_list compatibility adapter
permissions: A code does not enroll a student: an active student must already have ordinary course access
A teacher holding a valid code may be added to teacherIds; administrators already satisfy ordinary access
Listing ignores caller-supplied role and enforces user_id equals the signed-in account; created_by_id only narrows the authorized result
state_changes: Connection adds teacher membership only when not already authorized, then invalidates list and teacher-scope caches
Non-student listing has a 30-second per-user/role cache and in-flight coordination; student listing re-reads roster authorization rather than using that TTL
No student assignment or browser state is created by either route
success: POST /api/agents/connect-by-code normalizes the six-character code, resolves the TA and reports already_joined
GET /api/azure/agents/list delegates with authenticated user.id and user.role; force_refresh requests a refresh and created_by_id filters the returned list
Cosmos membership metadata is primary and hidden meta-agents are filtered; only admins/superadmins can use the unscoped Foundry-list fallback
failure_retry: Unknown code is 404; unassigned students or identity mismatch receive 403; persistence failures are 503
Student/teacher list failures fail closed instead of falling back to an unscoped remote list
Reconnect after success returns already_joined rather than granting another role; listing is repeatable
No code-based student self-enrollment, share-token conversion or cancellation workflow exists

workflows.title: Administrator course placement
agent_tools: None; conditional Cosmos course patch
permissions: AdminUser checks global active administrator role, not graph-memory scoped administration
Course/job discrimination rejects records containing job_type
Placement strings are validated as a complete institute/department pair or both empty; they are not checked against a directory membership registry
state_changes: PUT sets institute and department, clears departmentId, and invalidates agent-list caches without invalidating teacher scope
No roster, graph-memory identity or browser storage is changed
success: GET /api/agents/{agent_id}/placement returns a revision and placement, falling back from institute to legacy institution
An incomplete stored pair is returned as two empty strings
PUT the same path verifies revision, patches with IfNotModified and returns the new revision
failure_retry: Invalid saved values are 422; missing course is 404; stale revisions are 409; operational failures are 503
Reload after uncertain success or conflict; repeated writes with stale revisions are not silently replayed
No cancellation or automatic roster reassignment

workflows.title: Course Companion form assistance
actors: Active teachers, administrators and superadministrators editing a course form
agent_tools: Existing named agent form-fill-assistant, version 4; not CACA or a per-course TA
Local bounded text/document extraction and image normalization; lifespan-owned Responses client
The local agent_definition declares no tools, but assist_course_form references an existing remote version rather than publishing that definition
permissions: Only teacher/admin/superadmin roles are allowed; no existing-course membership check is made
Returned prerequisites must match the request's availablePrerequisites plus __none__; this catalog is client supplied
allowEdits=false forces all returned fields to null
state_changes: No course, agent, material index or learner-memory record is persisted; store=False on model request
The caller may apply returned fields to its form; the router does not write browser state
Local extraction intermediates and normalized images are request-scoped; the client closes on lifespan exit
success: POST /api/course-form/assist validates text, draft, short history and up to three attachments
form_agent_input extracts bounded TXT/Markdown/DOCX/PDF text or normalizes static images; no OCR or course-material upload
The named version is called with a 90-second timeout and no SDK retries; completed output is validated as CourseFormResult
failure_retry: Invalid requests or rejected attachments are 422 with form-preserving messages; unavailable/incomplete/invalid model output becomes 503
No automatic model retry, durable job, server-side undo or cancellation endpoint; retry the unchanged form request
A successful response is a suggestion, not course creation; the declared gpt-5 model constant is not proof of the remote version's deployed configuration

workflows.title: Local material acceptance checks
agent_tools: None; material_uploads.inspect_material uses local PDF, document and image validation
permissions: require_teacher rejects students; preflight does not require a particular course or draft
state_changes: None in durable storage or browser storage; only upload streams and local inspection results
success: POST /api/knowledge/preflight accepts multipart files, checks 1-100 files and 250 MiB per batch, then returns per-file accepted/errors and limits
PDFs are bounded to 100 MiB and 2000 pages; non-PDF indexing inputs are at most 16 MB; supported types are explicitly allowlisted
Hashes, source IDs, sanitized stored names, page/OCR indicators and preparation requirements are computed without indexing
failure_retry: A rejected individual file remains a per-file result; invalid batch limits are 422 and other failures are mapped to 409/503
Inspecting again is side-effect-free; an OCR indicator does not mean OCR was performed
No durable job or cancellation operation is created

workflows.title: Owned material drafts and original uploads
actors: Active course owners, assigned teachers and administrators
agent_tools: None; material_jobs and Blob originals persistence
permissions: Students are rejected
An unattached draft requires its exact owner; an attached job requires course edit access and matching session
knowledge_build with agent_name resolves the authorized course session instead of trusting a caller-selected destination
state_changes: Deterministic Cosmos material job per owner/request_id; immutable original blobs marked AzureSearch_Skip
Manifest entries, source identity, generation and job upload status persist with revisions
No browser storage or search-ready claim is made by upload
success: POST /api/knowledge/drafts creates or returns an owner-bound deterministic material session
POST /api/knowledge/build accepts multipart files/session/kb_scope and optional agent_name, validates each original, stores it and checkpoints the job
Repeated unchanged source uploads reuse their existing entry; processing is a separate action
failure_retry: Unsafe files are 422; changed/leased/processing batches are 409; service errors are 503
Uploads are processed sequentially, not atomically: earlier files may remain after a later file fails
Retry the same draft request ID and original files, then inspect status; no upload rollback or cancel endpoint

workflows.title: Durable material processing, polling and events
actors: Authorized draft owner or course editor
agent_tools: No material-processing agent; leased material_jobs worker, prepared_parts, shared Search indexer and scoped search verification
A creation subjob may call CACA before material work; the worker is not itself an agent
permissions: All three endpoints require require_material_job: non-student, owned draft or editable course, matching material session
SSE checks authorization initially and again through each status read
state_changes: Cosmos checkpoints, five-minute renewable leases, attempts, file generations and index boundaries
Prepared Blob copies and Search documents; original uploads are retained
SSE connection state is process-local and does not own the durable job
success: POST /api/knowledge/jobs/{job_id}/process starts or resumes selected failed sources and recognizes already-running work
GET /api/knowledge/jobs/{job_id} returns normalized material and TA states
GET /api/knowledge/jobs/{job_id}/events emits status every two seconds for up to 600 iterations, stopping on terminal state or disconnection
Worker prepares deterministic copies, checks a fresh indexer execution and verifies every expected copy in the scoped index before declaring ready
failure_retry: Terminal jobs with in-progress phases are reported as stopped/failed, not indefinitely running
Worker failures back off and stop after four failures or a permanent error; indexing times out after two hours; unknown failed indexer parts fail closed
Retry failed source IDs through process; a successful file is not unnecessarily regenerated
Lifespan starts both material and curriculum workers, signals stop and research shutdown, waits for in-flight work, then closes clients; disconnecting SSE is not job cancellation

workflows.title: List, download and remove course materials
agent_tools: None; material manifest, Blob download and queued Search-copy removal
permissions: Listing and removal require non-student course edit access; download permits ordinary course access including enrolled students
Session comes from course setup; source_id downloads verify matching job, scope, filename and source
Filename/path constraints and private response headers do not make downloads public share capabilities
state_changes: Listing/download have no persistence writes
Removal records a remove operation in the durable manifest with progress=uploading; process must subsequently be invoked
Worker removal deletes indexed documents and prepared copies, retains original blobs and marks the source removed; no browser state is written
success: GET /api/agents/{agent_name}/course-materials lists original job sources plus supported legacy flat files, hiding prepared copies and pending removals
GET /api/agents/{agent_name}/course-materials/file streams the authorized original or legacy blob as an attachment
DELETE the file path with source_id and kb_scope marks a source for removal and returns job status
failure_retry: Missing file/job is 404; changed sessions or processing jobs are 409; storage failures are 503
An already removed source is returned unchanged; a queued removal is not complete until processing finishes
No generic arbitrary-path deletion, original-blob erasure or server cancel endpoint

workflows.title: Explicit common-index refresh
actors: Active course owners, assigned teachers and administrators
agent_tools: None; shared Search indexer and course_materials operation verifier
permissions: Both endpoints require course edit access; submitted session_uuid must equal course setup session
Status requires the currently stored operation ID and session, not an arbitrary indexing job
state_changes: Course materialIndexing snapshot stores a fresh operation ID, expected files and request time
Status GET can persist a changed operation state; shared indexer execution affects the configured common pipeline
No browser persistence is performed
success: POST /api/knowledge/update-index saves an operation and requests the common indexer
GET /api/knowledge/index-status verifies unchanged files, a successful execution newer than the request and exact scoped filename coverage
failure_retry: Changed files produce changed; execution failures or 15-minute timeout produce failed
Missing/stale operation is 404/409; unavailable pipeline is 503
Each POST creates a new operation rather than using an idempotency key; recheck status before retrying; there is no indexer-cancel endpoint

workflows.title: Durable CACA-assisted course TA creation
agent_tools: CACA is the named course-agent-creation-agent specification generator with tool_choice=none
Application code unifies prompts, builds tools and creates a named Foundry prompt TA; no separate LACA, TCA or LearningAgent is inferred
Hosted memory preparation is skipped whenever the global graph-memory feature is enabled
permissions: Creation requires a non-student and the exact material-draft owner; createdById cannot name another account
Status and retry use require_material_job: owned unattached draft or matching editable course
Model/search configuration is normalized against server settings; reservation and creationJobId/course_job_id bind ownership
state_changes: Name reservation, input digest, phase checkpoints, attempts and uncertain-create marker in Cosmos
Applicable hosted memory store, named TA version, Blob setup and Cosmos course metadata
Metadata caches invalidate; curriculum work is queued when textbooks are present; no learner mastery or browser storage is created
success: POST /api/agents/create-async queues the owned draft; GET /api/agents/creation-jobs/{job_id} reports progress
Preparing generates validated description/instructions and optional hosted memory independently; creating confirms or creates the owned remote TA; saving persists course metadata
POST /api/agents/creation-jobs/{job_id}/retry resumes failed checkpoints
The result distinguishes TA completion, knowledge_pending/material status and later curriculum readiness
failure_retry: Same normalized request digest returns existing work; changed request/name ownership conflicts are 409
Malformed/incomplete CACA output is rejected, not accepted as raw instructions; bounded retry backs off and stops after four failures or permanent failure
A started but unconfirmed remote create is reconciled by owned-agent lookup, not blindly duplicated
Stopped parent jobs are surfaced as creation failure; explicit retry preserves successful phases; no cancellation, rollback or cross-service transaction

workflows.title: Legacy curriculum editing, status and research recovery
actors: Active course editors updating or retrying
agent_tools: No agent on status or manual PUT
Research job invokes main._background_textbook_research or main._background_threshold_concept_research; those reference CACA and configured textbook/threshold research agents
The durable worker and curriculum persistence are application code, not agents
permissions: GET requires ordinary course access; status_only suppresses curriculum content, not authorization
PUT requires non-student course access and matching optional user_id; authoritative graph mode rejects this legacy mutation with 409
Retries require course edit access; textbook and threshold aliases retain the same checks
state_changes: PUT saves legacy curriculum and optional commit-message history, stripping _status/_error and invalidating cache
Canonical curriculum JSON is overwritten in Blob; Cosmos pointer/timestamp update is best-effort and a pointer failure does not undo the saved Blob
Research jobs save durable status, leases, attempts and inputs; downstream helpers save curriculum/research output; complete curricula are cached and partial ones evict their cache entry
Graph publication or graph-memory activation is not performed; no browser state is directly changed
success: GET/PUT /api/agents/{agent_name}/course-curriculum read status/content or save manual edits
POST /api/agents/{agent_name}/course-curriculum/retry queues eligible failed/not-available work; retry-textbook-research is its compatibility alias
POST /api/agents/{agent_name}/retry-threshold-research requires locally saved syllabus research and queues threshold-only work

Full research reframes a syllabus through CACA, enriches textbook/module coverage through the configured textbook agent, then batches threshold/misconception/example-question proposals through the configured threshold agent

Module outputs are merged and normalized; legacy curriculum, raw artifacts and initial history are saved where applicable; worker checks complete persisted syllabus plus threshold concepts before marking success
failure_retry: Ready/processing work is returned without duplicate queuing; incomplete saved description/textbook or missing threshold-only input is 422
Worker uses five-minute renewed leases, retries a failed research run up to two attempts, then needs explicit retry; research helpers have their own inner streaming/batch retry and split behavior
Status distinguishes not_available, processing, failed and ready; partial curriculum is not readiness and generated question examples are not approved graph diagnostics
Storage/queue failures are 503 and require status recheck; canonical Blob failure is fatal while Cosmos pointer failure is warning/nonfatal
ResearchShutdown derives from BaseException and bypasses broad Exception retry/finalization handlers; interruption can retain the prior durable checkpoint and lease until recovery
Normal shutdown signals the process-local flag and cancels queued shared-executor futures; neither action forcibly cancels an in-flight remote request, and no user-facing cancel endpoint exists

Version-history save and curriculum save are not one transaction; retry handlers do not perform the PUT handler's explicit authoritative-mode guard, and legacy research recovery is not reviewed graph publication

workflows.title: Shared-default and private-custom syllabus translations
actors: Active authorized course members, including enrolled students
agent_tools: Direct configured CHAT_MODEL Responses calls, not a named agent; strict TranslationBatch output
Blob result cache and renewable per-result lease; lifespan-owned model client
permissions: Ordinary course access and existing syllabus are required
Default-instruction translations are shared within the authorized course; custom instructions are keyed to the authenticated user
Requested source_hash must match current syllabus; language/style and instruction hashes are validated
state_changes: Versioned translation blobs keyed by course, source hash, language, style and instruction fingerprint; custom keys also include user hash
Lease heartbeat is process-local; neither original curriculum nor browser storage is changed
success: GET /api/agents/{agent_name}/course-curriculum/translations lists shared default and caller-custom results
GET the /{language}/{style} suffix returns an exact saved variant
POST the base path reuses a valid result or translates bounded string batches, validates complete coverage and saves an immutable result
failure_retry: Missing syllabus/result is 404; changed source or busy/lost lease is 409; oversized syllabus is 413; model/storage failure is 503
At most 800 source strings and 80000 characters; batches up to 80 strings/10000 characters, 90 seconds per call within a 180-second overall deadline, max_retries=0
Retries use the same cache identity; failed partial batches are not a successful saved translation; there is no durable translation job or cancel endpoint

workflows.title: Typed TA chat, compatibility adapters and actual harness
actors: Active authorized course members on legacy courses
Enrolled student accounts on graph-enabled courses
agent_tools: Per-course named TA through harness.runtime.GeneralAgent; base_agents.general_agent aliases the same module/cache; extracted dispatch/output/events/telemetry/turn_policy helpers perform their respective mechanics

Stateless add_message, add_document, add_quiz, add_challenge, add_circuit, add_slides, ask_clarification, suggest_next_queries, declare_plan, get_threshold_concepts and update_topic_progress tools; batches use up to six tool threads
add_circuit runs the simulator and add_slides performs render preflight before emitting blocks; those are not asset saves
add_tikz_diagram calls configured generator/discriminator/polisher chat-completions models and local compilation; named-agent labels/provisioning helper are not the executed reference path
generate_image calls the configured image model and Blob/quota helpers; course-document grounding uses session-filtered Search
The harness contains a direct web-search helper, but both production stream adapters hardcode web_search_enabled=False; accepted request fields do not activate it
Graph observation extraction/reduction/worker are separate from the TA; the optional post-stream Content Safety progress-claim check logs diagnostics and does not block or rewrite output
permissions: require_agent_access plus active-account validation; body.user_id must equal the account
Graph capture rejects teacher/admin preview, requires a stable non-operation_ event_id and strict learner/course/scope authorization
Both graph modes bind/verify conversation metadata; authoritative ingress additionally rejects unverified hosted memory and pins the remote version
The legacy conversation-ID branches do not perform that graph-scope metadata check
Graph-scoped dispatch blocks teacher analytics and _LoggingQueryTool also refuses whenever global memory is enabled; the global-disabled legacy logging branch has no corresponding caller-role check
state_changes: Foundry conversation/messages/tool outputs and shared endpoint-agent-session cache; per-turn learner identity stays request-local
The delegated main._load_setup_json can migrate a local setup or reconstruct metadata into Blob during chat preparation; this is not the read-only Blob loader used by require_course
Graph-enabled ingress durably records learner input and optional private image artifacts before inference; receipt headers expose event ID/status
Legacy progress tools can update Cosmos state; authoritative progress tool is read-only, while shadow retains legacy progress writes
SSE done additionally infers up to three legacy in_progress topics from turn text in off/shadow; AG-UI omits this inference and authoritative mode suppresses it
Both streaming adapters persist usage best-effort and may start a nonblocking progress-claim diagnostic; graph nonstream aggregation does not use those adapter wrappers
Image generation consumes quota and attempts Blob persistence; local diagram/circuit/render intermediates and clarification waits are not durable jobs
These router functions do not themselves save browser state or provide a whole-turn idempotency record
success: POST /api/agents/{agent_id}/chat/stream or /chat/agui delegates to main SSE or AG-UI adapters after prepare_chat; SSE has its own setup and AG-UI uses _open_agent_stream
POST /chat/start or /chat/continue uses legacy nonstream helpers when memory is off; with memory context it consumes _open_agent_stream and aggregates selected blocks
Both stream entry paths ignore the payload web_search_enabled field by forcing false; research_mode only forces tool_choice=required and does not launch a deep-research agent
Streaming harness builds answer-depth/profile/saved-research/course context, emits preparing then ready, calls the TA and dispatches tools, plans, clarifications, citations and usage
Existing suggestion events are moved after answer content; greeting starters are deterministic, not an extra general inference call
Graph-enabled quiz tools freeze server instances in both shadow and authoritative modes; only authoritative mode injects graph context as the state authority
failure_retry: Empty text/images is 400; unsupported depth or missing continuation/event ID is 422; identity/scope violations are 403
Memory acceptance failures fail the HTTP request before model execution; same event ID/input reuses the ledger receipt, but replay can still produce another model response
Tool errors cancel placeholders and return correction output; bounded plan-step rewind is not a global tool-round limit
Final tool-output persistence failure emits an error; some follow-up exceptions break the loop and can still reach done, so done is not proof all requested work succeeded
Image quota-store failure currently allows inference, and Blob failure can leave an inline-only image; an unknown nonretired function currently gets success-like output without an implementation
Both stream adapters use a daemon producer, one-slot queue and 15-second SSE comments; consumer cleanup sets stop but does not forcibly cancel a running model/tool/clarification call
No router cancellation endpoint or transaction rolls back accepted evidence/tool writes when the browser disconnects

workflows.title: Independent course-grounded follow-up suggestions
agent_tools: GeneralAgent.generate_next_queries uses a direct configured chat-model Responses call, not a TA conversation or separate agent
Greeting-only requests use deterministic course-name starters
permissions: require_course applies ordinary membership and resolves the material session; the submitted question/answer is request context, not a learner-state write
state_changes: None in durable learner or conversation storage; cached GeneralAgent may be initialized; no browser storage is written
success: POST /api/agents/{agent_name}/chat/suggestions loads course name/description and calls the follow-up generator
The generator truncates question/answer context, requests strict CourseSuggestions JSON with store=False and returns queries
failure_retry: The direct call uses eight seconds and no automatic retries; incomplete/invalid/model failure returns an empty query list
Course/client setup failures outside that fallback become 503; authorization errors remain their original HTTP errors
Suggestions can be retried independently without re-running the completed answer; no durable job or cancel endpoint

workflows.title: Owner-only clarification waits and answer windows
actors: Active account owning a pending clarification
TA harness waiting for tool answers
agent_tools: ask_clarification tool plus process-local clarification_registry; no new agent
permissions: Every endpoint authenticates the current active account and checks registry ownership
No course ID is accepted here; ownership derives from server-side tool registration
Exactly one answer entry per registered question is required; empty answer strings are allowed
state_changes: In-memory answers, monotonic deadlines, revision and submitted flag guarded by a threading.Condition
No durable clarification job or browser persistence; the wait removes its entry on completion
success: GET /api/clarify/{clarify_id} returns private no-store timer/status; PATCH saves a draft; POST submits answers
POST /api/clarify/{clarify_id}/extend requires the current revision during the decision window and starts another answer window
The harness flushes the clarify event before waiting, then feeds submitted or timeout-retained drafts back to the same turn and emits clarification_done
failure_retry: Wrong owner is 403; expired/submitted/missing wait is 410; stale or premature extension is 409; answer shape is 422
Default answer window is 60 seconds plus a ten-second decision window; extension is revision checked, not an automatic refresh
Process restart or another worker cannot recover this registry; worker affinity matters
Registry cancel is an internal helper, not an HTTP route; repeated submission after acceptance is 410, and client disconnection alone is not a durable cancel

workflows.title: Bounded owner-created transcript shares
actors: Public token holder through the separately owned read-only main handler
agent_tools: None; owner-partitioned Cosmos thread/message persistence
permissions: Authenticated identity, not query user_id, selects the owner partition; conflicting user_id is 403
The selected saved message IDs must be nonempty, unique and a subset of the owner's latest persisted messages
A share token does not confer course membership, learner-memory access, editing, tool execution or roster rights
state_changes: Thread shareToken, sharedAt, sharedMessageIds, sharedTitle and updatedAt are saved
refresh explicitly updates the boundary while retaining the existing token; revoke removes sharing fields
No model call, learner-memory write or browser storage mutation
success: POST /api/chat/thread/{thread_id}/share returns an existing token unchanged unless refresh=true, otherwise saves the explicit selection boundary with conditional replacement
DELETE the same path disables later token-based reads; absent owner thread returns success=false
Public reading uses the saved ID boundary, or a validated original share time for legacy links, rather than automatically including future messages

main.get_shared_chat selects top-level thread/message fields and re-signs eligible generated images; content, metadata and imageUrls remain in the response rather than undergoing blanket recursive privacy redaction
failure_retry: Unsaved/invalid selections or conditional write conflicts are 409; missing owner thread is 404; backend failures are 503
Existing-token non-refresh requests reuse the prior boundary rather than revalidating and extending it
Revocation is not ETag-conditional and does not recall copies already downloaded; read-only presentation is not automatic redaction of user-authored prose
No share job or cancellation endpoint

workflows.title: Frozen server-graded assessments and legacy quiz passthrough
actors: Enrolled student for graph-enabled assessment scope
agent_tools: TA add_quiz freezes an assessment before these endpoints; HTTP grading itself is deterministic, not another model or agent
MemoryService grading, immutable ledger and private compatibility asset cache; observation extractor runs later
permissions: Signed-in identity must match optional userId, with ordinary course access
When global memory is enabled and course mode is shadow or authoritative, strict current learner/course/curriculum/epoch access is required
Graph-enabled saves/submissions require quizId equal to server-issued assessmentInstanceId and matching curriculumVersion; submissions require non-operation_ event_id
state_changes: Server-frozen keys and catalog mappings stay in learner-scoped assessment records; public pre-submission quiz omits keys/explanations
First submission, answer-exposure records, input event, receipt and sequence cursor commit together
A separate private quiz/attempt asset is a repairable cache, not the grading or memory authority; no browser state is written
success: POST /api/quiz-assets uses canonical server title/questions for enabled memory; GET /api/quiz-attempts/{quiz_id}/first reports frozen submission status
POST /api/quiz-attempts/first grades only submitted problemId/selected/reason against the frozen instance, ignoring browser keys, correctness, text and misconception claims
Published approved catalog tasks can qualify for diagnostics/transfer; generated questions remain non-qualifying practice

Global disabled/course off delegates to main's legacy helpers: _normalize_first_quiz_attempt compares selections against caller-supplied correct indices, enriches concept mappings best-effort and saves one deterministic private first-attempt asset
failure_retry: Bad identity/scope is 403, invalid instance/input is 422, changed graph curriculum or conflicting graph first answer is 409
On graph paths, same normalized answers return the saved first submission and original event receipt; changed answers conflict
The legacy asset path instead returns the existing first attempt even for a different valid later submission, with up to three conditional-write attempts
If compatibility asset persistence fails after graph ledger acceptance, retrying the same submission repairs the cache
Later use of an already exposed answer is marked answer-revealed; grading does not itself certify mastery
No first-submission overwrite, job cancellation or evidence deletion endpoint

workflows.title: Persist quiz feedback without granting grading authority
agent_tools: None in this route; main.append_quiz_feedback_endpoint stores caller-supplied feedback
permissions: Same identity and course checks as assessment routes
With memory enabled for the course, the frozen first submission must exist before feedback is accepted
The optional assessmentInstanceId does not replace the path quiz_id lookup or grant a different learner scope
state_changes: Sets the first nonempty compatibility attempt asset agentFeedback and updatedAt; later feedback is left unchanged
No direct authoritative memory state mutation or browser write
success: POST /api/quiz-attempts/{quiz_id}/feedback checks access and optional frozen-submission precondition, validates the legacy request and delegates to main
Despite append naming, append_quiz_agent_feedback is first-feedback-wins and retries conditional conflicts up to three times
failure_retry: Enabled-memory pre-submission feedback is 409; missing submitted asset is 404; backend errors follow memory error mapping
No event_id receipt is exposed, but an existing feedback value is reused even when a later request supplies different text; inspect saved feedback after uncertainty
Feedback prose is not an observation, server grade or threshold verdict; no cancellation endpoint

workflows.title: Self-service learner instructions
actors: Any current active account editing its own learner profile
agent_tools: None; profile persistence
Later TA turns may consume customInstructions as scoped preferences, not system policy
permissions: The account ID comes only from authentication; no target-user parameter or cross-account read/write
Private no-store responses; identity and write acknowledgements are verified
state_changes: PUT replaces customInstructions and updatedAt in the authenticated user's profile
Subsequent harness turns replace prior injected preference snapshots; existing remote agent instructions are not updated
The router itself writes no browser storage
success: GET /api/learner-profile returns the caller's current instructions, normalizing null to empty
PUT the same path saves validated instructions and verifies the returned identity/content/timestamp
failure_retry: Missing profile is 404; storage or inconsistent acknowledgement is 503
No ETag or idempotency token is exposed; retry/read back after an uncertain save; empty instructions are an explicit clear
Harness failure to remove stale injected snapshots stops a later turn rather than claiming the new preferences took effect; no profile-save cancel endpoint

workflows.title: Typed self-only legacy learning view
actors: Active authorized course member viewing their own saved legacy learning data
agent_tools: None; typed profile and legacy learning-state reads
permissions: require_agent_access applies ordinary course membership; user identity always comes from the active account
Stored learning-state key, course, partition and user identity fields are checked before returning data
state_changes: None; private no-store read; this route does not initialize legacy progress or switch to graph-memory projection
success: GET /api/learner-profile/learning/{agent_id} returns ok plus typed legacy progress or no_state, and a list containing the nonblank saved preference if present
failure_retry: Missing profile is 404; storage/identity/schema failures become 503
Repeatable read with no durable retry or cancel operation
Do not equate this compatibility record with authoritative graph evidence or threshold crossing

workflows.title: Opt-in memory scope, mode and activation
agent_tools: No new agent; graph service and conditional course replacement
Authoritative activation reads the existing remote TA definition to reject hosted-memory tools; it never silently edits that definition
permissions: Global GRAPH_MEMORY_ENABLED defaults false; PUT requires it enabled
Admin/superadmin role alone is insufficient: account must appear in the exact tenant/institute scope registry, including initial binding
Existing memory_scope is immutable; active course actor and registry checks apply
A non-off mode requires a published, teacher-reviewed graph matching institute and course; authoritative additionally verifies hosted-memory isolation
state_changes: Conditional replacement updates server-owned memory_scope, curriculum_binding and graph_memory_mode; metadata/teacher caches invalidate
No graph is published, evidence migrated or learner snapshot mutated by configuration; no browser state write
success: GET /api/agents/{agent_id}/memory/config returns enabled, mode, optional bindings, revision and role-based can_manage hint
PUT the same path checks scope, graph, isolation and revision, then activates off, shadow or authoritative
Shadow captures/processes graph evidence but retains legacy teaching context/progress behavior; authoritative uses graph context and read-only legacy progress tools
failure_retry: Disabled feature is 404; unauthorized scope is 403; immutable scope, unpublished graph, hosted memory or stale revision is 409; unverified service state is 503
can_manage is a coarse role hint, not proof that PUT will authorize
After uncertain replacement reload configuration; no automatic publication, activation, remote-memory removal or cancellation

workflows.title: Scoped curriculum graph drafting and legacy import
agent_tools: None; deterministic import_legacy_curriculum, graph validation and draft persistence
permissions: Global memory feature, active course, editing actor, immutable memory identity, scope registry and curriculum binding are required; students are rejected
Draft graph tenant/curriculum must match binding, institute set must equal the authorized institute and any course restrictions must include this course
An authorized editor can work on another version of the same bound curriculum; this does not activate it
state_changes: Mutable graph draft is forced to DRAFT/published_ready=false and stored under conditional revision
Legacy import constructs a reviewable draft; original curriculum and learner records are not rewritten
No browser persistence is performed
success: GET /api/agents/{agent_id}/course-curriculum/graph returns the requested/bound draft, falling back to a published graph with revision=null
PUT the same path validates and saves a draft with expected_revision
POST the /import suffix converts a complete legacy curriculum with threshold concepts into the requested graph version
failure_retry: Missing draft/graph is 404; incomplete legacy curriculum or draft revision conflict is 409; invalid/over-budget graph is 422
Published versions cannot be edited: create a new draft version
Import is not model research, assessment approval or activation; retry against the latest revision, with no cancel operation

workflows.title: Reviewed immutable graph publication
agent_tools: None; graph policy validation and immutable graph/catalog persistence
permissions: Same strict editor scope as graph drafts; expected course and draft revisions must match
reviewed must literally be true; server supplies reviewer and review time
state_changes: Published graph version and version-catalog record; no course binding/mode change, learner replay or browser write
success: POST /api/agents/{agent_id}/course-curriculum/graph/publish or compatibility /course-curriculum/publish validates the exact draft
Server adds review metadata and policy review flags, validates publication readiness and appends immutable graph/catalog records
A separate scoped-admin memory/config update is required to activate the published version
failure_retry: Revision changes or conflicting immutable content are 409; invalid publication policy is 422
Same-reviewer retry reuses existing review time to support identical-content publication; graph and catalog writes are separate repairable immutable writes
The request event_id is required by the schema but not consumed as an operation receipt; publication is not a queued learner event
No unpublish, cancel or automatic activation endpoint is present

workflows.title: Scoped learner snapshots, context, evidence and receipts
actors: Assigned teacher reading an active explicitly enrolled student
agent_tools: None on reads; bounded graph retrieval, committed snapshots, evidence and processing receipts
permissions: Global feature, non-off course mode, active course, reviewed scope registry and current binding/epoch required
Student cross-target is denied before metadata/registry reads; teachers/admins require active student target in explicit roster including promoted-invitation aliases
Individual-depth context rejects students; student context removes misconception nodes, DIAGNOSES edges and observations; direct evidence clears misconception_ids
Snapshot endpoint returns the typed snapshot without the context endpoint's diagnostic redaction; do not claim uniform redaction
state_changes: No persistent read-side mutation; freshness is a conservative derived view and pending work remains separate
Artifact response is private attachment/no-store; no browser storage is written
success: GET /api/agents/{agent_id}/learners/{student_id}/memory returns mode, snapshot, freshness, pending_count and next processing receipt
GET /memory/context builds bounded ta or individual context; GET /memory/evidence/{evidence_id} reads scoped evidence
GET /memory/evidence/{evidence_id}/artifact streams an existing private evidence artifact
GET /memory/events/{event_id} returns a receipt, optionally from an earlier authorized learning_epoch within the current binding
failure_retry: Disabled/off is 404; wrong actor/roster/scope or future epoch is 403; missing evidence/receipt is 404; invalid/budget input is 422; backend/integrity failures map to 503
Empty initialized views mean no evidence, not mastery; pending or stale state must not be treated as current
Repeatable reads with no cancellation operation; no arbitrary Blob path or cross-curriculum-history selector is exposed

workflows.title: Verified teacher evidence and asynchronous state derivation
actors: Assigned teacher or registered scoped administrator submitting verified student work
agent_tools: No teacher-evidence agent; MemoryService accepts evidence
FoundryObservationExtractor is a configured model call with tools=[] and tool_choice=none, followed by deterministic state/threshold/profile reducers
MemoryProcessor is a leased application worker, not an agent
permissions: Strict editable learner scope and active explicitly enrolled target; student writers are rejected
verified_learner_work must be true; TC/problem IDs must exist in the published graph
Server binds teacher identity and event namespace; raw model summaries are not accepted mastery writes
state_changes: Immutable learner input plus receipt and sequence cursor; actor-scoped event identity
Worker persists evidence, validated observation sets, transitions and an atomically published snapshot/receipt
No browser write or direct state-setting API
success: POST /api/agents/{agent_id}/learners/{student_id}/memory/events returns 202 receipt after durable acceptance
Worker builds catalog-derived evidence, extracts grounded observations, validates quoted source spans and approved rubric/task references
Deterministic reducers assess independence, assistance, recency, misconception clearance and transfer before any crossing
Publication commits snapshot, transition and completed receipt together; teaching/chat alone is not a certified demonstration
failure_retry: Same actor/event/input is idempotent; changed input under the same event identity is 409
Worker model refusal, invalid output, storage or reducer failure retains the last committed state and retries with backoff up to configured attempts
Worker is separately disabled by default: accepted inputs can remain pending when GRAPH_MEMORY_WORKER_ENABLED=false

Main lifespan conditionally starts the worker, signals stop and waits up to 30 seconds before task cancellation; durable leases/receipts permit recovery, not guaranteed termination of an in-flight thread
No endpoint directly sets mastery or cancels accepted evidence

workflows.title: Audited retry and deterministic memory revalidation
actors: Assigned teacher or registered scoped administrator
agent_tools: No recomputation agent; failed-input retry audit, system-revalidation event and deterministic replay
Observation model may run only if a retried earlier input still lacks its immutable extraction
permissions: Strict editable learner scope; students cannot recompute
Only current epoch may reopen failed input; failed next receipt is selected server-side, not an arbitrary caller-selected record
state_changes: At most one retry audit per operation identity resets the next failed input to pending and clears attempts/lease/error
New ordered system-revalidation event and receipt; worker derives snapshot from retained evidence/observations
No browser write, score override or deletion
success: POST /api/agents/{agent_id}/learners/{student_id}/memory/recompute or /memory/recomputations derives a server operation identity from graph and supplied event_id
It attempts audited failed-input recovery, returns any existing operation receipt, otherwise accepts revalidation
Worker enforces sequence order and renews leases; expiration scheduling also creates deterministic revalidation events without an HTTP endpoint
failure_retry: Same operation returns the prior receipt; conflicting scope/input is 409; disabled/unauthorized access is 404/403
A failed earlier event blocks later sequences rather than being skipped; exhausted retries require a new authorized recovery operation
Saved extractions are reused, partial immutable evidence can remain after failure, and snapshot publication stays atomic
No user cancel endpoint or automatic success on model/parse failure

workflows.title: Queued learner reset into a new learning epoch
agent_tools: None; reset event and deterministic worker epoch publication
permissions: Strict learner access; teachers are explicitly denied even if they own the course
Students can reset only self; administrators need the reviewed scope registry and active enrolled target
state_changes: Reset input/receipt is accepted in the current stream; processing creates a new epoch and empty snapshot while retaining historical evidence/artifacts
Old scoped conversations no longer match the new epoch; no browser state is directly cleared
success: POST /api/agents/{agent_id}/learners/{student_id}/memory/reset accepts a stable event_id-derived operation
Repeated operation returns the saved receipt; immediately previous-epoch receipt recovery supports retry after the reset was applied
Worker publishes reset transition, receipt and next epoch state atomically when its sequence becomes eligible
failure_retry: 403 for teachers/cross-target; 409 for older-epoch identity conflicts requiring the original receipt; service failures use memory error mapping
202 means queued, not immediately reset; earlier pending/failed events and disabled worker can delay it
History is never deleted; no reset cancellation or implicit replay of old evidence into the new epoch

workflows.title: Explicit-roster memory cohort summaries
agent_tools: None; canonical roster resolution and bounded committed-snapshot aggregation
permissions: Students are rejected; active course, non-off mode, current binding and scope registry are required
Roster is course studentIds plus promoted-invitation canonicalization, never discovered chat participants
Only active student profiles survive resolution; duplicate canonical identities are collapsed and oversized roster queries fail
state_changes: None; no evidence is loaded and no snapshot is mutated; no browser persistence
success: GET /api/agents/{agent_id}/memory/cohort or /api/teacher-dashboard/memory/cohorts/{agent_id} returns bounded aggregates with optional tc_id and offset
Response includes coverage, complete/partial, unassessed/stale counts, curriculum/policy identity, next_offset and per-student rows
failure_retry: Unknown TC/offset or roster limits are 422; unauthorized course/scope is 403; disabled/off is 404
A capacity-limited later page may return partial results with next_offset; consumers must not present partial coverage as a full cohort
Returned rows contain authorized student IDs, not anonymous-only data; repeats are read-only and there is no cancel job

workflows.title: Progress compatibility reads and reset branching
actors: Course teachers or administrators subject to mode-specific rules
agent_tools: None; main legacy progress helpers or graph read-only projection/reset queue
permissions: Every branch authenticates and checks ordinary course access; students cannot target another user
Authoritative reads additionally enforce strict enrolled-learner scope; authoritative reset denies teachers and requires stable event_id
Off/shadow branches delegate without the authoritative target-roster check; course access is not equivalent to authorization over every student's graph memory
state_changes: Authoritative GET is a read-only compatibility projection, not a legacy-state initialization
Authoritative POST queues a new learning epoch and retains history
Off/shadow GET calls ensure_learning_state and may create legacy state on first read; off/shadow reset deletes legacy learning state and invalidates its cache
No browser write by these wrappers
success: GET /api/agents/{agent_name}/progress/{user_id} returns graph-derived threshold projection only in authoritative mode; otherwise main.get_learning_progress ensures state and returns summary plus full topics/objectives or no_state

POST /api/agents/{agent_name}/reset-progress/{user_id} queues graph reset with a body in authoritative mode; otherwise main.reset_learning_progress deletes legacy state, which can be initialized again on a later read/chat
failure_retry: Authoritative body omission is 409 with instruction to use memory/reset; ordinary identity errors are 403
Graph reset retries follow operation/epoch receipt semantics; legacy reset has no equivalent receipt and delegated exceptions can remain HTTP 500
A repeated legacy reset can erase progress recreated since an earlier reset; it is not the graph epoch/idempotency contract
Compatibility threshold percentage is a projection, not a second memory authority; no automatic mode migration or cancel route

workflows.title: Explicit circuit tool enablement and schema update
agent_tools: No model inference; Foundry named-agent version inspection/mutation for add_circuit
Shared 60-second Blob tool-update lease and local ngspice availability check
permissions: require_tool_owner requires course edit access plus createdById ownership or admin role; assigned co-teacher alone is insufficient
Local simulator must exist before enabling/updating; TA must be prompt based
state_changes: New remote agent version replaces/adds add_circuit while preserving other tools/metadata/description
Metadata cache invalidates; lock blob/lease exists; no learner or browser state writes
success: GET /api/agents/{agent_name}/circuit/tool reports enabled, update_available, engine_available and latest agent_version
POST the same path acquires the lease, reads latest version, checks status and expected_version, then explicitly creates a new version
failure_retry: Already-enabled/current tool returns unchanged before expected_version comparison; otherwise stale version or non-prompt TA is 409
Missing simulator is 503; contention 409/412 maps to 409; uncertain remote write is 503 with instruction to recheck
No SDK retry on create_version, no automatic provisioning during simulation, and no disable/cancel endpoint

workflows.title: Bounded educational circuit simulation
actors: Active authorized course members, including students
agent_tools: None in this endpoint; deterministic typed netlist builder and local ngspice subprocess
TA AddCircuitTool validates and runs the same simulator before producing its initial circuit/result block; neither path accepts arbitrary learner code
permissions: Ordinary course access; simulator request need not be owner-only or have the remote tool enabled
Typed components, identifiers, bounded values, topology and analysis are validated; no caller-supplied raw netlist/command
state_changes: Process-local semaphore and transient simulator files/output; no persistent asset, memory or browser write
success: POST /api/agents/{agent_name}/circuit/simulate validates CircuitSimulationRequest, resolves course access, generates a netlist and runs ngspice
Parsed bounded results are returned for the caller's circuit; optional prlimit constrains supported hosts
failure_retry: Invalid circuit/solver failure/timeout is 422; missing or busy simulator is 503
Subprocess timeout is eight seconds; raw output size and parser limits are checked; slot releases in finally
Retry busy runs later or simplify unsolved circuits; no durable simulation job, cancellation endpoint or hardware-safety claim

workflows.title: Explicit presentation tool enablement and schema update
agent_tools: No model inference; named-agent add_slides tool version inspection/update
Uses the same Blob tool-update lease as circuit controls
permissions: Owner or administrator plus course edit access; assigned co-teacher alone cannot change the remote tool
expected_version must match latest, and a changed tool requires a prompt-based TA
state_changes: New remote TA version containing current add_slides schema/description; metadata cache invalidation
No deck, learner state or browser storage is created by enablement
success: GET /api/agents/{agent_name}/slides/tool compares latest tool against the local definition
POST the same path leases the update, checks expected_version, returns unchanged if current, otherwise updates/adds add_slides preserving other definition data
failure_retry: Unlike circuit, stale expected_version is checked before the already-current no-op
Stale/non-prompt/contention is 409; unconfirmed service write is 503; recheck tool status before retrying
No automatic tool update from a local schema edit, no create_version retry, no disable/cancel route

workflows.title: Validated PowerPoint export and private presentation copies
agent_tools: None in these endpoints; typed SlideDeck validation and local render_presentation
TA add_slides is a separate content-producing tool, not the export or asset persistence operation
permissions: Ordinary course access, including enrolled students; remote add_slides enablement is not required
Deck has bounded slides/layout/text/notes/source URLs; asset owner is authenticated user and is_public=false
state_changes: Export generates response bytes only; save creates a new slidesId and private presentation JSON asset
No original shared/received deck is overwritten and no browser state is written by the server
success: POST /api/agents/{agent_name}/slides/export preflights layout and returns editable PPTX with private no-store attachment headers
POST /api/agents/{agent_name}/slides/save uses the same render preflight, creates a private JSON copy and returns its assetId/block
failure_retry: Overcrowded layouts are 422; preparation/persistence failure is 503
Export can be repeated without a durable write; save has no idempotency key and each successful retry creates another copy
An uncertain save asks the caller to inspect assets before retrying; no export/save cancellation endpoint

workflows.title: Course-authorized slide voice catalog and narration
agent_tools: No agent or script-writing model; allowlisted Indian English/Hindi Speech voices and bounded text-to-speech request
permissions: require_speech_course checks active account/course membership before speech body parsing
Only validated text and allowlisted voices; SSML is built/escaped server-side rather than accepted from the caller
state_changes: No durable audio, deck, learner or browser storage; cached settings and request-local bounded MP3 bytes only
success: GET /api/agents/{agent_name}/slides/voices reports static voice catalog and configured availability with private no-store
POST /api/agents/{agent_name}/slides/speech synthesizes the supplied script and returns audio/mpeg without exposing the service credential
failure_retry: Invalid body is 422; missing configuration/authentication is 503; invalid upstream response is 502; timeout is 504
429 propagates bounded Retry-After of 1-60 seconds; requests are not automatically replayed
Two MiB audio and 30-second stream deadline bounds apply; no persisted audio job or cancellation endpoint

workflows.title: Authenticated browser voice-input token exchange
actors: Any active signed-in account using voice input
agent_tools: None; service identity token acquisition and Speech STS token exchange
permissions: get_current_active_user is required; the migrated token route is not public
No course or teacher-only authorization; resource/region come from server settings
state_changes: No durable learner/course record; token and region returned privately for caller use, no browser storage written by the router
success: GET /api/speech/token verifies configured resource and region, exchanges a service identity credential at the configured Speech resource and returns a bounded nonempty token with no-store
failure_retry: Unconfigured speech or failed token exchange becomes 503; missing/invalid account remains 401/403
Exchange uses a ten-second HTTP timeout and disables redirects; underlying identity helper may retry credential acquisition
Repeat requests obtain tokens rather than replay a durable result; no transcription, model call, job or cancellation endpoint is performed here
